rationale: Mapped the full landscape over 5 trained configs: iter0 depth6/lr0.05/279f=0.16417 (baseline), iter1 depth8/lr0.05/279f=0.16326 (best), iter2 depth4/lr0.05/279f=0.16608, iter3 depth8/lr0.02/279f=0.16447, iter4 depth8/lr0.05/141f(FS prune)=0.16497. Findings: (1) train_val_gap <= 0.02 every iteration => NO overfit; (2) depth response over {4,6,8} spans only 0.00282 and lr scan adds nothing => HP CEILING, no config beats baseline by more than the ~0.001 noise floor; (3) FS prune (279->141) raised val_brier +0.00171 vs the same unpruned config => FS is neutral-to-harmful on this non-overfit cell, exactly the rule-1 prediction; best model keeps the full 279-feat pool. Stopping per agent judgment (agent_should_stop): depth+lr+FS exhausted, ceiling confirmed. NOTE: I attempted a monotone-constraint ablation (iter_4 decision with monotone_constraints +1 on 21 vol estimators) but the agent_file_protocol decision validator (loop_protocol.validate_decision) rejects monotone_constraints as a non-whitelisted HP — it is only passable via spec hp_starting on a fresh launch, not via a resume decision file. So the monotone_contraindicated check will SKIP for this run; the contraindication itself is already established for this exact cell in the _147 study + the tuning playbook (rule 4).
